newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Profit-taking pushes Swedish shares lower.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking pushes Swedish shares lower.

text.p: Profit-taking nudged Swedish shares lower on Tuesday with most sectors ending on a softer note, although underlying sentiment remained positive.
Forestry shares slipped most, depressed by concerns about NorScan pulp stocks data.
The exchange's general index fell 0.35 percent to 2785.47 in turnover of 4.95 billion crowns.
"It was a bit nervous here during the afternoon and trade felt rather thin both yesterday and today...it seems as if the market is ripe for some profit-taking," a broker said.
But sentiment was positive and no large drop was expected.
The forestry sector dropped 1.07 percent. Concerns ahead of NorScan pulp stocks data and the sector's weak performance in the U.S. weighed on sentiment.
MoDo lost 3.5 crowns to end at 240 crowns, SCA fell five to 173 crowns, Stora slipped 0.5 crown to 107.5, while AssiDoman rose 1.5 to 207.5.
Heavyweights telecoms group Ericsson and drugs major Astra were pulled along in the general fall. Ericsson ended two crowns lower at 270.5 and Astra fell 2.5 crowns to 373.5.
